correctness.rationale: Every shattered edge support has an all-positive geodesic witness; coordinate transitivity reduces it to canonical path edges. Local forced-edge implications forbid both endpoint pairs and three consecutive positions. Reversal within free coordinate blocks realizes every requested trace under exactly those conditions. Triple/pair index partitions give the VC ceiling floor(2d/3) and a periodic support attains it. For Ldim, fixing a positive edge query factors the remaining path family into independent disjoint-domain smaller cube geodesic classes. The standard product upper bound by induction forces all positive branches to depth ≤d−2. An explicit two-next-coordinate adaptive tree of depth d−1 proves equality. The d=1 boundary is handled. Independent direct and subset-state enumerations agree for d≤9, the support criterion is checked through d=12, and every leaf of explicit trees through d=11 is replayed. The exact all-dimensional theorem is proven mathematically, not inferred from this finite evidence.

value.rationale: The problem is intrinsic to learning which of d! symmetric shortest cube paths is hidden using local edge-incidence queries. The theorem classifies every shattered support relative to a witness path, gives sharp dimensions in every cube dimension, identifies the first adaptive/static separation at dimension four and an unbounded gap asymptotic to d/3. These are structural, quantitative distinctions between static and adaptive identification on a canonical infinite family, not an arbitrary small-instance census.
